Paper Title: MMBS: Towards Robust Visual Question Answering: Making the Most of Biased Samples via Contrastive Learning
Authors: Qingyi Si, Yuanxin Liu, Fandong Meng, Zheng Lin, Peng Fu, Yanan Cao, Weiping Wang, Jie Zhou
Problem Addressed: Trade-off between OOD and ID accuracy when penalizing biased samples
Method & NLP Mechanism: InfoNCE contrastive loss on positive samples generated via word Shuffling (random permutation) and prefix Removal (string deletion)
Dataset & Backbones: VQA-CP v2, VQA v2 | UpDn, BAN, LXMERT, LMH, SAR
Main Result: UpDn+MMBS: 48.19% on OOD (+8.45%), 63.84% on ID. LMH+MMBS: 56.44% on OOD, 61.87% on ID (+5.52%).
Inherent Limitation: Random word shuffling breaks syntax; prefix removal creates headless fragments. UpDn+MMBS drops from 48.19% to 42.80% on natural test questions.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: How to eliminate question category priors without corrupting the grammatical syntax and sequential transition dynamics of the language model?
Takeaway for Project Direction: Anchor Paper establishing the OOD/ID dilemma; highlights the critical need for syntax-preserving sample transformation.

Paper Title: DDG: Digging out Discrimination Information from Generated Samples for Robust Visual Question Answering
Authors: Zhiquan Wen, Yaowei Wang, Mingkui Tan, Qingyao Wu, Qi Wu
Problem Addressed: Critiques MMBS: word shuffling and removal destroy question grammar and semantics
Method & NLP Mechanism: Multi-modal Knowledge Distillation transferring discrimination information from positive/negative samples rather than rigid latent contrast
Dataset & Backbones: VQA-CP v2, VQA v2 | UpDn, SAN
Main Result: 61.34% (UpDn) and 63.28% (SAN) on VQA-CP v2, surpassing MMBS without extra annotations.
Inherent Limitation: Still feeds syntactically corrupted question strings into the network; relies on distillation loss to smooth over the noise.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Bypassed the linguistic destruction with distillation rather than repairing question syntax at the input source.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Verifies that grammar destruction is a recognized bottleneck, but attempts to fix it at the loss level rather than NLP parsing.

Paper Title: CopVQA: Causal Reasoning through Two Cognition Layers for Improving Generalization in Visual Question Answering
Problem Addressed: Debiasing models require massive synthetic data augmentation and large models
Method & NLP Mechanism: Cognitive Pathways decomposing interpretation and answer generation across 2 causal cognition-enabled components (CCs)
Dataset & Backbones: VQA-CP v2, PathVQA | Modular Expert Networks
Main Result: 60.78% on VQA-CP v2 and SOTA on PathVQA with only 25% of the parameter count of prior SOTAs.
Inherent Limitation: Treats question Q as an unparsed black-box vector in causal routing; ignores internal syntactic structure.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Fine-grained linguistic compositionality and internal question structure (word order, dependency relations) remain completely unmodeled.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Proves that modular causal routing is highly parameter-efficient, but language understanding remains a monolithic black box.

Paper Title: KDSR: Robust Knowledge Distillation and Self-Contrast Reasoning for Debiased Visual Question Answering
Authors: Ke Ning, Rongrong Shen, Zhixin Li
Problem Addressed: Uniform in-batch negative samples in MMBS are trivial and provide weak contrastive gradients
Method & NLP Mechanism: Self-Contrast Reasoning and Knowledge Distillation to tighten negative contrastive decision boundaries
Main Result: Outperforms MMBS by +6.49% on VQA-CP v2 while improving VQA v2 performance.
Inherent Limitation: Focuses purely on the negative sample branch; keeps MMBS heuristic word perturbations for positive samples.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Language quality of the positive question remains noisy; word order corruption is left unresolved.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Confirms that negative sample hardness matters, but positive sample syntactic corruption is still neglected.

Paper Title: MCCD: Look, Listen, and Answer: Overcoming Biases for Audio-Visual Question Answering
Authors: Jie Ma, Min Hu, Pinghui Wang, Wangchun Sun, Lingyun Song, Hongbin Pei, Jun Liu, Youtian Du
Problem Addressed: Unimodal biases extend beyond vision to audio and video modalities
Method & NLP Mechanism: Multifaceted Cycle Collaborative Debiasing across audio, video, and text on newly curated MUSIC-AVQA-R
Main Result: Establishes SOTA on AVQA debiasing benchmark, mitigating unimodal shortcuts across audio and video.
Inherent Limitation: Tailored to audio-visual synchrony; textual question processing reuses standard unparsed encoders.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Question-level linguistic bias is left unresolved; multimodal alignment does not solve sentence syntax bias.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Demonstrates how debiasing principles expand into new multimodal domains while text processing remains primitive.

Paper Title: Robust Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Methods, and Future Challenges
Authors: Jie Ma, Pinghui Wang, Dechen Kong, Zewei Wang, Jun Liu, Hongbin Pei, Junzhou Zhao
Problem Addressed: Lack of unified theoretical framework and taxonomy across VQA debiasing research
Method & NLP Mechanism: Comprehensive taxonomy categorizing methods into Ensemble, Data-Balanced, Causal, and Contrastive branches (MMBS as anchor)
Dataset & Backbones: All VQA Benchmarks (VQA-CP, GQA-OOD, VQA v2)
Main Result: Formalizes the OOD/ID trade-off dilemma and establishes standardized comparative baselines.
Inherent Limitation: Survey paper providing analytical taxonomies without introducing a new empirical mechanism.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Points out that the community is trapped in an artificial trade-off without a method that eliminates priors while preserving natural language.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Authoritative proof that contrastive debiasing is an enduring paradigm, and that the OOD/ID trade-off is an active open problem.

Paper Title: Task Progressive Curriculum Learning for Robust Visual Question Answering
Authors: A. Akl, Abdelwahed Khamis, Zhe Wang
Problem Addressed: Drastic distribution shifts cause catastrophic forgetting of in-distribution knowledge
Method & NLP Mechanism: Curriculum learning dynamically scheduling training samples from biased (easy) to unbiased (hard/OOD)
Main Result: Modest improvements (+1-2%) on VQA-CP v2 without sacrificing ID performance.
Inherent Limitation: Does not alter the language encoder architecture; relies purely on sample presentation order.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Underlying language shortcuts remain intact; the model merely delays memorizing biased samples.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Shows that sample scheduling alone is insufficient to break language shortcuts without architectural/linguistic intervention.

Paper Title: CC-VQA: Towards Robust Visual Question Answering via Causal Intervention and Contrastive Learning
Problem Addressed: Contrastive learning learns statistical representation correlations rather than true causal invariance
Method & NLP Mechanism: Front-door and back-door causal adjustment integrated with contrastive latent representations
Main Result: Outperforms MMBS by +5.26% on UpDn backbone.
Inherent Limitation: Causal adjustment operates on high-level latent embeddings; confounders are estimated from coarse question types.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Causal intervention operates at the latent embedding layer; the token-level linguistic source of prior is untouched.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Hybrid causal-contrastive models work well, but still treat the question as a global semantic vector.

Paper Title: CLAP: Overcoming Language Priors via Contrastive Learning and Answer Perturbation
Authors: Haoquan Wang, Yong Chen, Shengbo Chen, Hong Rao
Problem Addressed: MMBS relies on external data augmentation heuristics that damage sentence fluency
Method & NLP Mechanism: Dictionary-based answer perturbation generating contrastive pairs without external data synthesis
Main Result: Reaches 62.0% on VQA-CP v2 without requiring external synthetic sample generators.
Inherent Limitation: Intervention is concentrated on the answer space and static dictionary lookups rather than question parsing.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Bypasses question syntax corruption by intervening on answers, leaving internal question understanding unresolved.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Proves contrastive learning works without heavy data generation, but leaves question language modeling unimproved.

Paper Title: Counterfactual Dual-Bias VQA: A Multimodality Debias Learning for Robust Visual Question Answering
Authors: Boyue Wang, Xiaoqian Ju, Junbin Gao, Xiaoyan Li, Yongli Hu, Baocai Yin
Problem Addressed: Single-modality debiasing fails to isolate dual biases (visual shortcut + question prior)
Method & NLP Mechanism: Multimodality counterfactual contrast generating counterfactual question-image pairs as hard negatives
Dataset & Backbones: VQA-CP v2, VQA v2 | UpDn, SAN
Main Result: Reaches 61.3% on VQA-CP v2, tightening multimodal decision boundaries.
Inherent Limitation: Counterfactual question generation uses crude dictionary swapping (antonyms, random objects), often breaking grammar.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Lacks linguistic minimal-pair constraints that preserve grammatical constituency; text counterfactuals violate natural syntax.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Highlights the power of hard counterfactual negatives, but exposes the lack of linguistic grammar control.

Paper Title: DSI: Dual-Space Intervention for Mitigating Bias in Robust Visual Question Answering
Authors: Runmin Wang, Xingdong Song, Zukun Wan, et al.
Problem Addressed: Existing methods conflate dataset-level distribution shift with instance-level linguistic bias
Method & NLP Mechanism: Dual-Space Intervention projecting representations into Language Bias Space and Distribution Bias Space
Main Result: Achieves 62.2% on VQA-CP v2 with UpDn, setting a top benchmark among non-pretrained backbones.
Inherent Limitation: Mathematical separation occurs at linear projection layers; language encoder still receives unparsed raw text.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Language representations are still vulnerable to n-gram shortcuts because the input text pipeline is unchanged.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Represents the mathematical ceiling of latent-space debiasing; proves that further gains require input-level NLP parsing.

Paper Title: Mitigating Distribution Shift via Adaptive Reweighting for Robust Visual Question Answering
Authors: Xingdong Song, Runmin Wang, Han Xu, et al.
Problem Addressed: Uniform debiasing penalties over-regularize unbiased samples and under-penalize biased ones
Method & NLP Mechanism: Dynamic gradient-based adaptive reweighting allocating loss weights based on model uncertainty
Main Result: Surpasses static loss baselines on OOD benchmark while maintaining competitive ID accuracy.
Inherent Limitation: Optimization-level trick; treats bias as a scalar weight, ignoring linguistic and visual semantics.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Does not address question understanding; models can still fail on grammatically complex questions.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Confirms that loss re-weighting has reached diminishing returns without linguistic semantic intervention.

Paper Title: OSCAR: Online Self-Calibration Against Hallucination in Vision-Language Models
Authors: Minghui Chen, Chenxu Yang, Hengjie Zhu, Dayan Wu, Zheng Lin, Qingyi Si
Problem Addressed: In Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs), language priors cause open-ended generative hallucinations
Method & NLP Mechanism: Online self-calibration via Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) lookahead with Dual-Granularity Reward + DPO
Main Result: Significant reduction in hallucination rates across open-ended generative vision-language tasks.
Inherent Limitation: Extremely compute-intensive (requires A100 GPU clusters); focuses on token decoding policy.
What did this paper leave unresolved?: Does not solve structured question parsing; complex multi-clause compositional questions still suffer from attention misallocation.
Takeaway for Project Direction: Proves the problem lineage from MMBS authors: language priors in small models evolve into hallucinations in large models.
